title: The Doctrine of the Mean
lines: What Heaven has conferred is called Nature.
Accordance with this Nature is called the Path.
Regulation of this Path is called Instruction.
The Path may not be left for an instant.
What can be left is not the Path.
The gentleman is cautious where he is not seen,
And apprehensive where he is not heard.
There is nothing more visible than what is hidden,
And nothing more manifest than what is subtle.
Therefore the gentleman is watchful when he is alone.
Before feelings of pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arise,
When these feelings arise and each attains due measure,
Equilibrium is the great foundation of the world.
Harmony is the universal path of the world.
Let equilibrium and harmony reach their full development,
And heaven and earth will be in their proper places,
And all things will be nourished.
